text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The purpose of the next formal round of United Nations talks at Montreux next week is for the two sides to agree on an agreed text outlining the guidelines towards a comprehensive solution to the Cyprus dispute.
- British army declares Ayia Napa out of bounds after attack on tourists.
- The Cyprus pound touches new lows against the dollar and sterling, but the central bank dismisses fears of an impact on the economy.
- Investors in Woolworth express concern that plans to seek a listing on the Athens Stock Exchange could harm the concerns of local shareholders.
- Cyprus is interested in buying Iraqi crude, says refinery chairman Yiannis Leondis.
- The government provokes the feelings of the public by forgetting about the actions of those who instigated the coup in Cyprus in 1974.

- The government feels the best way to continue the procedure towards solving the Cyprus problem is for the two sides to submit their positions in writing on all aspects of the Cyprus problem by the end of 1997.
- Former President Spyros Kyprianou steps up his calls for the prosecution of Lt-General Phaedon Ghizikis, the Greek "President" of the junta which engineered a coup on the island in 1974.
- The Auditor General calls for order in cooperative credit societies after recent disclosures of mismanagement which has resulted in the accumulation of millions in bad debts.
